issues.description: Constructor signature and attribute mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the Problem Statement UML and the example instantiations in the template Main expect Animal and its subclasses to have only a 'name' attribute and single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). The solution implementation adds an 'age' attribute to Animal and defines constructors for Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat that require two parameters (String name, int age). This divergence means the provided example Main code and the UML-provided design will not compile/run against the solution classes and will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures and attributes consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Revert the solution to match the UML and template Main by removing the 'age' attribute from Animal and changing Animal/Seal/Pig/Goat constructors to a single-parameter signature (String name), updating implementations accordingly; or (B) Update the problem statement (UML, task text) and the template Main examples to document and use the new 'age' attribute and two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Ensure the chosen design is reflected in the UML, the problem description, the template Main usage examples, and all provided solution/template classes so students are not blocked by mismatched constructor signatures.
